_note: One template shape scaled by hours: about two thirds on the current modules and review (module, review, gesture and long sessions), about one third on invention tied to the current module. Tuesday and Thursday are jiu-jitsu evenings, so they hold short optional sessions only. The app fills each session from the learner's current modules, not fixed weekday topics.

weekly_templates.name: 3 hours a week: keep the thread
weekly_templates.description: Four sessions on Monday, Wednesday and the weekend; Tuesday and Thursday stay free for jiu-jitsu, with the 10-minute short session as an option. About two thirds goes to the current module and its review, one third to drawing it from imagination. A missed session is dropped, not stacked onto the next day. This is the default plan.

sessions.focus: Current module: a 5-minute warm-up from its ongoing drill (lines, ellipses, boxes or 30-second gestures), one lesson section or resource, then its exercise. Stop on time.
Warm-up, then one or two due revisits drawn cold and checked against their chapters' checks, then 15 minutes of the current module's drill.
Apply the current module in one longer drawing from life or reference, then check it with a flip, an overlay or a greyscale photo and note the main error.
Draw this week's subject from imagination in new views and combinations, then check it against reference (40 minutes). Finish with 20 minutes of free invention from a prompt.

weekly_templates.name: 6 hours a week: steady progress
weekly_templates.description: Five sessions plus an optional short one after Thursday training. The current module gets two weeknight sessions, a gesture session and a long Saturday block; invention gets Friday and most of Sunday. A missed session is dropped, not stacked.

sessions.focus: Current module: warm-up from its ongoing drill, one lesson section, then the exercise with one named technique on screen.
The gesture ladder for 15 minutes, then 30 minutes on the current module's exercise from reference.
Optional, after training: the 10-minute short session or two due revisits. Skip if tired.
Invent with this week's module: draw its subject from imagination from two new viewpoints, then check against reference and mark what you guessed.
One long application of the current module from life or reference, with a check at each stage (block-in, values, finish) and an overlay or greyscale check at the end.
60 minutes of invention tied to the module (combine, redesign or stage this week's subject in a small scene, then check it), then 25 minutes of free drawing from a prompt.

weekly_templates.name: 10 hours a week: push hard
weekly_templates.description: Daily sessions with long weekend blocks. Monday, Wednesday and Friday get an hour or more; Tuesday and Thursday after jiu-jitsu hold short optional sessions only. Saturday is structured long work; Sunday is mostly invention with a short review. Drop to the 6-hour plan in any week work gets heavy.

sessions.focus: Current module: warm-up, one lesson section, then the exercise; a second exercise if the first is done.
Optional, after jiu-jitsu (about 20:15): the 10-minute short session, or box and ellipse warm-ups plus one revisit.
The gesture ladder or a figure session for 30 minutes, then 50 minutes of the current module from reference.
Optional, after jiu-jitsu: draw something you saw today from memory, then check it against a photo, or two due revisits.
Invent with this week's module: new views, combinations and redesigns of its subject from imagination, each checked against reference.
Three one-hour blocks on the current modules: a long application from life or reference, a construction or perspective project, and an observational study with an overlay check.
90 minutes of invention tied to the module (a small scene or design built from this week's subjects, checked against reference), then 40 minutes of free drawing from prompts.
Review: due revisits drawn cold, then pick the week's best and worst drawing and write one line on what to change next week.
